verdict.rationale: Statsig documents its own environment-tier isolation. Development and staging environments use environment-specific SDK keys that set which rule sets download, and development, staging and production data are kept separate, so a user can test outside production. Isolation is by environment tier within the same project, not a dedicated sandbox account, and only one doc item describes it. missing for 10: a dedicated sandbox project or account isolated from production configs, detail on how agents or API/CLI calls target non-production environments, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: evaluate feature gates, dynamic configs, and experiments differently in non-production environments like development or staging
Isolation is by environment tier and key, not a separate sandbox account.
